correctness.rationale: For an even n≥4, all nonempty proper Walsh coefficients vanish under (n−1)-wise fair independence; inversion gives exactly μ(s)=2^−n(1+θ∏s_i), |θ|≤1. Expanding the nth even moment, the unique monomial surviving multiplication by the top character uses each sign once, giving precisely θ n!∏a_i; lower even orders are ordinary independent moments. For fixed squared length S, conditional two-coordinate averaging q_i,q_j with fixed sum raises q_iq_j; in the explicit 2k moment expansion all coefficients of (q_iq_j)^r are nonnegative, with h=k≥2 a strictly positive linear coefficient, so unequal squared magnitudes strictly reduce the independent-sign moment. AM–GM bounds |∏a_i| by (S/n)^(n/2) with rigid equality and θ sign alignment. Thus (M_n+|θ|n!)/n^(n/2) is sharp with exactly equal nonzero magnitudes and product-sign alignment (unless θ=0). Even-cycle Walsh edge products realize θ=1. Independent exact arithmetic reproduces θ=1 n=4,6,8 constants 4,124/9,71; finite verification is not an infinite proof.
risks: The theorem is even n and real coefficients only; nothing claimed for non-even moments or smaller independence.
